steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Any clues on the Sarcophagus?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: The very latest activity we know of involving the Sarcophagus came after the Chernobog-Lungmen incident, when the Ursine government retrieved the entire system.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: As for what they actually plan to do with it, they've been keeping it under tighter wraps than ever. There's nothing more about it in Kal'tsit's records.

options: It's not like we can directly ask the Ursine government to borrow it...
Do we have any other way of finding its location?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Looking at the official register made after the Chernobog research institute was destroyed, there were no survivors other than Sergei.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: We did manage to find some clues when looking into what happened to him afterwards.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: He had established a new institute to continue researching the Sarcophagus. In the short period of time that the institute was operating, one name really stood out to us—

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Artyom Chaadayev.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: He was vice-director at Sergei's institute, but he's a complete ghost, with no verifiable academic or political background to speak of.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: We may be able to make a rational deduction...

options: That this man had a special connection to Sergei?
That this man had a special connection to the institute?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: No matter what his connection may be, he might be the key to our breakthrough.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: So we need to find this Artyom?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: No, things get a little more complicated from here on out...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: He's proven to be very hard to track ever since Sergei's institute shut down.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: According to Kal'tsit's intelligence, he died of heart failure in the Grypherburg Imperial Sanatorium last winter.

options: He maintained a good relationship with Ursus to his last.
Maybe we can look into the people who knew him.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Great idea! That's what I was thinking too.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: There's another researcher who had a connection to Artyom.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Ksenia Markovna Nelidova.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: We have a lot more detail on her background. Before the Sarcophagus incident, she had briefly served as Ilia's assistant at the Chernobog research institute, and had crossed paths with Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Recent intelligence indicates she is currently in the Ursine Far North, working at the Central Mining District Laboratory, administered by the city of Bresk.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: That's where Artyom's final letters were sent.

options: It doesn't sound like a particularly reliable clue...
But it's the only clue we've got.
We should go to the research institute and find her.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I have to remind you, Doctor.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: While we're all determined to bring Kal'tsit back, we must thoroughly evaluate the risks of every mission.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Rhodes Island cannot bear any more losses.

options: But...

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I'll go.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Raidian?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Ursus has always been a dangerous place, and we have very limited intelligence for this mission.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: And there are many important decisions the Doctor and Amiya must make while Rhodes Island is being rebuilt.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Raidian, I can—

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I know you're a capable young woman now, Amiya, but that is exactly why you need to stay here and handle our most important tasks.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: The latest news from Laterano is also worrying, and the Doctor will need to see to it personally. Allowing Rhodes Island to steady its footing in our new home is our top priority.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You're right...

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: If it were just an infiltration mission, then Misery's team would be the best choice, but information gathering is my team's specialty.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Besides, there's no one better to send back to Ursus than me, is there?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You make some real compelling arguments, Raidian...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But it's your decision, Doctor.

options: This will be a very dangerous mission.
Stay safe, Raidian.
Rhodes Island cannot lose anyone else.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: We will. We'll act with caution as a mobile medical team.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: The rest of you, take care of yourselves while we're out, okay?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Of course...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I hope that all of you come home safe.

steps.name: Wizened Voice
steps.text: '...I shall meditate and share in his pain.'

steps.name: Wizened Voice
steps.text: 'One man's pain is everyone's pain, one man's sin is everyone's sin...'

steps.name: Wizened Voice
steps.text: 'May sinners repent with all their heart, may their sins be forgiven, and their souls find salvation...'

steps.name: Pained Howling
steps.text: Wargh—!

steps.name: Pained Howling
steps.text: Ahhhhhh—!

steps.name: Elderly Woman
steps.text: Oh my...

steps.name: Young Miner
steps.text: It's... okay, ba-babushka. D-Don't... be scared.

steps.name: Young Miner
steps.text: It's U-Uchitel Rankin... He's chased away the P-Patrol Unit chasing us.

spans.text: Rankin... He's chased away the P-Patrol Unit chasing us.

steps.name: Young Miner
steps.text: We're s-safe for now.

steps.name: Elderly Woman
steps.text: Yes... for now.

steps.name: Elderly Woman
steps.text: Where else can we go? Where must we go to find shelter...?

steps.name: Young Miner
steps.text: B-Babushka... are-are you hungry...? I'll go ask Hawley... for another piece of bread.

steps.name: Elderly Woman
steps.text: I'm fine... You're such a sweet child, but I really am.

steps.name: Elderly Woman
steps.text: Go see Rankin.

steps.name: Elderly Woman
steps.text: He has done so much, his spirit must be nearly worn away.

steps.name: Elderly Woman
steps.text: Go see him. Do not let him be burdened any more than he already is.

steps.name: Young Miner
steps.text: Uchitel, he...

steps.name: Youthful Miner
steps.text: Phew...
Under the twilight sky, the young man's stern countenance eases.
The cold soon cools the warm blood staining his pickaxe. The enemy before him is completely routed.

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Don't... Don't kill me! You're not allowed to do anything to me, I surrendered!

steps.name: Youthful Miner
steps.text: But we haven't accepted that surrender.

steps.name: Youthful Miner
steps.text: Tell me, how many of these squads are pursuing us?

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Chyort! I don't—I don't know!

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Every Patrol Unit's independent, we don't talk to each other!

steps.name: Youthful Miner
steps.text: Tell me something I don't know, or I'll have no reason to let you live.

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Wait, don't! Listen to me!

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: The chips you have in you! The diagnostic chips!

steps.name: Youthful Miner
steps.text: Chips? You mean the ones used to check how infected we are?

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Ha... Hahaha...

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: 'Rankin the Noble', 'Rankin the Hero', are you really so naive?

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Those chips send your coordinates to the mine's research facility and nearby guard posts. The moment you try and leave the mining district, or the chip leaves your body—

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Boom!

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Losing a single leg would be lucky. Losing both is definitely possible. You won't be running anywhere like that, haha!

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Just give up already, Rankin... You think you can leave this mine by killing a Patrol Unit?

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: There's nowhere to go. Ursus will chase you forever.

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Surrender. It's the only way you won't die a miserable death.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: Don't listen to him, Rankin! If the chips really did blow up, we'd have a bunch of three-legged burdenbeasts walking around!

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: The Patrol Units are worse than bastards! An honest one of them is like an aphid in winter! I got to know them before I became infected!

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Gah—!

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: You've done enough today, Rankin. Leave this one to me!

steps.name: Young Miner
steps.text: N-No!

steps.name: Young Miner
steps.text: St-Stop—killing people!

steps.name: Young Miner
steps.text: We don't... need to! N-Nobody's... badly hurt...

steps.name: Young Miner
steps.text: Uchitel!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Let him go.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: Get back, Vetochki! What's the point in showing a man like him mercy?

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: It was these bastards who killed Paulina, all because she was caring for an unregistered child... She was pregnant when they hanged her!

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: Have you forgotten all the terrible things they've done?

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Urgh! *cough* *cough*

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: Haha, thank you, Vetochki.

steps.name: Frightened Patrol Unit
steps.text: I remember you... You were the meekest of all the children. You will have a happy ending, even if the rest of these scum—

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Uchitel!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: ...At least I didn't let him bleed out slowly in the snow.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Stand up, Vetochki. Go to the back and find that doctor for me.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Paul, go get Nikto and tell him to gather everyone who wants to leave the mining district at the south dormitory.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Get them ready, we need these chips out of us.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: You believe what that guy said?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Doesn't matter, we need the chips out of our bodies. Even if they don't explode, they definitely transmit our location.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: The Patrol Units have already found us once, and we don't know when the next squad will show up. If this keeps on, we'll be on the back foot the entire time.

steps.name: Excited Miner
steps.text: Alright, I'll get it done.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Uchitel, y-you pro-promised... me...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Oh, you're still here.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I didn't promise you anything, Vetochki.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Besides, if the rest of the bastards in his units are dead, why should he be any exception? Because of his arrogance? Because of his ridicule?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: ...Never mind. You wouldn't understand. Forget what I just said.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Right, take this.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: What... is it?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: A stopwatch. I found it in the institute, should still work. When we get a minute, I'll teach you how to use it.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: From now on, you won't need to live your life counting meaningless numbers, worrying about a miscount leaving people dead in the mines.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: At least now... Go, Vetochki. Go help me find her.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Uchitel, your hand... is shaking...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Hush. Go do what you have to do.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: ...At least... let me...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Pray that your... soul... can be... saved.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Even though you've seen how those men treated us, and seen how I killed them?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Y-Yes.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Do not be so quick to bless others, or to forgive them, Vetochki. Me included.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Now go already. We don't have time.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: ...Gospodin Rankin.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Hello, Gospozha Serafina.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Though we have not known each other for long, I want to believe that, since your medical team was willing to come to such a remote place to treat the Infected, you are people I can trust.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I am sorry that I now have no choice but to ask for your help.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Please, go ahead. As long as it's something I can help with.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I just learned that inside every miner, there is a tracking chip that could explode at any moment. We need a way to extract them so we can escape the Patrol Units.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I am prepared to serve as a test subject myself.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: If it is successful, please perform the surgery on the others. If it does unfortunately explode, then I hope you will be able to give me first aid.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: If I die... then I ask you to tell everyone waiting for me about this.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Now, I must ask you to leave—

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: No. Let me do an examination first. May I?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: ...I regret to inform you, these chips really could explode.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: They contain miniaturized, high-powered Originium bombs. If the chip does not receive electrical signals from the local district relay or the human body, it will trigger an explosion...

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: If you hope to get everyone out of this district, then you must remove the chips.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Amazing. Is this your Arts at work?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Of course...

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I may be able to temporarily copy the signal to fool the receiver. But I must warn you, this still carries a great deal of risk.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We can't afford to wait for a perfect solution. Your idea is good enough.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: One moment, then.
Raidian starts using her Arts, causing beams of energy to resonate at the same frequency as the chip's receiver.
Rankin nods and sits down, grasping the hilt of his dagger. It is cold, smooth, and solid as he rubs it against the calluses of his palm.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: You'd best back away from me a bit, Doctor.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: That won't be happening. This is the first time I've tried it, so I need to observe it in real-time.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I can guide your hand using nerve impulses. Take care not to detonate the chip.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Incredible... It's a shame we didn't meet sooner.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I hope we will still have the chance to chat after this.
Rankin wipes his dagger with some alcohol, pointing its blade at the scar on his leg before plunging it into his flesh.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: ...It worked, right?
The youthful miner nearly leaps up, forgetting the cut on his leg oozing blood.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Calm down, your wound needs dressing.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Ah, of course. Thank you, Doctor. I owe you my life.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: You are truly amazing. I have never seen a physician as skilled as you. You even remind me of an Ursine soldier.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: What do you mean by that?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Sorry, please do not misunderstand me. This is the highest praise I can think of.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I mean true Ursine soldiers, not those Patrol Unit brutes. The ones who drove off the invading Nightzmora and freed us from the tyrannical Hippogryphs. They were true heroes.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Oh, yes, have you read Igor Velikiy's biography?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: We should prepare for surgery on the others. How many will we need to operate on?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I'm afraid it's a number that will leave you and your colleagues running ragged.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: My decoy electrical signal can cover the entirety of this area, and my colleagues can coordinate the surgeries. That being the case, I reckon we will need to stay here for some time.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Time is something we are short on.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Have the medical team prioritize the elderly and children, then teach the others to perform the surgery. Hand out some scalpels. My people are not squeamish.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I would appreciate it if you did not make medical decisions for me.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Ah, no, Doctor, I did not mean to order you around.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Since the duty of leading everyone out of this mining district is mine, I need to make decisions accordingly.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Patrol Units who can show up at any time, extreme weather, lack of supplies... All things that will prove fatal.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I hope we can reach an agreement on this.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: No matter what happens, we need to be wary of infection. My team will oversee the sterilization procedures.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Then let's begin.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: 'Act first, then discuss the future.'

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Blurghhh—!

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: *cough* *cough*! Blergh... *cough*!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Is this your limit?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: When you were eating smoked sausages back in Grypherburg, did you never wonder how they were made? Never went to see the slaughterhouses in the satellite cities?

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Idi nahui! Rot in hell, Rankin! Suka blyat'!

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: I swallowed a bunch of snow but I still can't get the smell of blood out of my nose. Next time I have the chance, I'm dumping fresh burdenbeast blood into your soup!

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: Fresh burdenbeast blood is expensive. A bucket can cost more than a hundred chervontsy, we can't afford that...

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: It was a metaphor, dammit... I didn't know you used to be a gourmet chef, Hawley.

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: My son transported that sort of thing when he was a truck driver. The Grypherburg nobles believed the blood of young burdenbeasts would make them beautiful.

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: He told me a lot of things about the city in his letters, but the last one I received was seven years ago. I hope he's still alright...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Then I'll have to ask you to make sure Nikto doesn't mess with my dinner.

steps.name: Hawley
steps.text: I'll make sure. Nobody is messing with anyone's dinner.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: I hope this won't end up being our last meal, or I'll be cursing you to the grave, Rankin.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Whatever you say. I'm in good spirits today.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: It's been so long since I've felt this sort of freedom.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We have finally broken our shackles. We are free now. What we want to do, where we want to go, and how we want to live our lives, we can decide for ourselves now.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: You should save the poetry recital for when we're actually safe...

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: So, what now?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: The plan hasn't changed.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: We head south to the border with Kazimierz, find the village founded by the Infected, the one that belongs only to the Infected. There will be space for all of us there.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: You're just blindly believing in this 'Reunion' without even knowing if they're the real deal...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: No, I have my reasons to believe.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: A few years back when I was stationed at the border, I heard a lot about them, information I could trust.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: They provide shelter for the Infected, give out medicine for free, and have fended off many Patrol Units who wanted to push around people like us. I believe we will find people who share our ideals there.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: That just makes me think it's some Infected delusion, or the army spinning up an excuse for a bigger share of taxes.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: It makes me wonder why it took until now for a banner like this to be flown.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: If... If we find out they do not exist, then it should be us who raise the flag.

spans.text: we find out they do not exist, then it should be us who raise the flag.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Hah... And here I thought your time on the border would have taught you better.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Just imagine for a moment, if you had saved that count back then instead of that Infected, you could be a lieutenant right now, maybe even a captain.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Patrol Units like the one we ran into today would be licking your boots with a wave of your finger.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Then I should be even more grateful for the choice I made that day. Otherwise, I would not have had the chance to see this nation's true face, or learn what my life's greatest calling is.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Our people have been duped and deceived for far too long! They believe their current lives are what they deserve, forgetting what they should really have!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: This is not only a conflict between the Infected and ordinary folk. If one day, all the Infected in Ursus died, they would use some other standard to decide who to cast into the mines.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Why do some have everything handed to them, while others must struggle for survival? Who do the fruits of their bitter toil go to?

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: But who actually gets to say what people deserve?

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Maybe the way this land is is the way things should be. Even if there were another Terra, even if civilization started over from scratch, things might not turn out any different from now.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: No... I don't believe that.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: When you opened your eyes and actually looked at everything around us, did you not feel anger? When we feel such an instinctual rage, that means everything is wrong!

spans.text: When you opened your eyes and actually
at everything around us, did you not feel anger? When we feel such an instinctual rage, that means everything is wrong!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: You should know that, based on what you've been through, Nikto.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Don't bring up that crap, it's ancient history...

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Fine... Even if it is as you say, how far are we from the border? What other things will we run into on the way there?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I have a plan. Why do you think I asked you to gather up those chips?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: They didn't blow up when we took them out of us like other chips, which means they still work as positioning devices.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: These things have brought us so much suffering. Why not use them to our advantage against the Patrol Units?

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: That's not what we agreed on when we decided to escape!

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: You know our condition, Rankin. How many of us can even move right now? Maybe half?

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: We might be able to beat one or two Patrol Units, but we can't hold off all of Ursus! The only thing causing more bloodshed would do is to trap us here even further!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: If we want to live, taking this step is only a matter of time.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Every Patrol Unit lackey we kill is another spare ventilator in our hands.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Any supplies we seize can be used to leave the icefields, and allow children like Vetochki to live to see another day.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Have you forgotten what gave us the opportunity to leave this place?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Even if that thing can't be called human, we were the ones who killed it.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: I don't know what you're talking about.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: You've become completely unreasonable, before we've even left the mining district!

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I don't want to fight over this, Nikto—

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Uchitel?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: And... Nikto, you're... here too...

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: N-Nothing. I just came to see if... you had eaten yet...

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Oh, you don't need to ask this guy. His stomach's already full of his grand ideals.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Haha... You're not really wrong.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: You should focus on our physician friends, it was they who did all the hard work today.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I just went to... see them. They're... about to... rest.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Good. You've worked hard too.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: How's the wound, does it hurt?

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: I... I'm okay. Everyone's... okay.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Really now? Everyone's been very brave.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Go rest. Eat your fill, then sleep tight.

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Eh... We... don't have much food... My portion's... not very big...

steps.name: Vetochki
steps.text: Take care of yourself... too... Uchitel...

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Vetochki really trusts you, Rankin, always calling you 'Uchitel', like you're her teacher.

spans.text: Vetochki really trusts you, Rankin, always calling you '

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Everyone trusts you. They're waiting for you to get them out of here.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: I know, which is why every word I tell her is what I know to be true in my heart.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: It is the same as when I lead everyone. I take the path I believe to be right.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Let's hope you are.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Relax a little, Nikto. Today is the day of our first victory. It's a good omen. No need to look so anxious.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: When someone awakens to the truth and decides to set off on a journey, it is the grandest of beginnings.

steps.name: Nikto
steps.text: Quoting from Igor's biography again?

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: No, those are my own words.

steps.name: Rankin
steps.text: Trust me, Nikto. We are doing great things right now.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Medic Operator
steps.text: All the surgeries are complete, Captain.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Medic Operator
steps.text: Some of the patients are developing fevers, and we're limited in what we can do...

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Got it. I'll go have a word with their leader after this, and do my best to ensure the wounded are provided with food and water.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: You've worked hard today. Get some rest. Taking care of yourselves is important too.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Medic Operator
steps.text: Captain, we still need to—

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: The Far North is under martial law, and the weather is affecting our ability to communicate too. It's difficult for us to connect to the outside.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: What happened here will surely draw the attention of the Ursine authorities. We need to leave ASAP. We can't stay here.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Medic Operator
steps.text: But do we really need to work with them?

steps.name: Rhodes Island Medic Operator
steps.text: I'm worried that if we do, we'll be drawn into a conflict with Ursus...

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Rhodes Island has no reason to make an enemy of the Empire, but right here, right now, these are just people struggling to survive.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Changing the lives of the Infected has always been our mission.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Besides, they have also helped us out a lot.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Don't worry for now, just do your best to prepare for the unexpected. I'll keep trying to get in contact with our base in the city.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: If they can receive the information we sent earlier... I hope they will notice the clues we left behind when they come to help us.

steps.name: Passing Newsboy
steps.text: Bresk Times, get your copy here—

steps.name: Passing Newsboy
steps.text: Do you want one, devushka?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Oh, s-sure. How much?

steps.name: Passing Newsboy
steps.text: Twenty para, is that okay?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: That's fine.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But I don't have any spare change on me... Here, take this.

steps.name: Passing Newsboy
steps.text: Thank you, devushka! You're amazing!
Amiya carefully places an entire chervonets in the boy's palm. He quickly disappears around the street corner, as if frightened his benefactor might regret her decision and take it back.

spans.text: in the boy's palm. He quickly disappears around the street corner, as if frightened his benefactor might regret her decision and take it back.

options: Amiya?
What're you looking at?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: That boy's clothes looked... very thin.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Bresk is colder than the Ursus I remember.

options: It was winter the last time we were in Ursus.
Bresk is further north than Chernobog.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I still remember...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It was the first time I saw such intense fighting. I was so nervous I forgot to be scared.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: At the time, I thought I would never see anything so dangerous again.

options: We've been through a lot since then.
At least now there's no Catastrophes or people chasing us.
At least now I know who I actually am.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: On that topic, Doctor, it's rather rare for us to have the chance to quietly watch a city like this, isn't it?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Chernobog, Lungmen, Londinium... Wherever we go, our memories seem to be filled with chaos and the fires of war.

options: It's how this land should be.
We should remember what this city is like now.
Let's check today's paper.
Does it say why the mines have been blocked off?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We might only be able to learn more once Eloysius has finished negotiating with the Grand Duchess.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: She said she would help us apply for a permit to enter the mining district, but how will she actually go about doing that?

options: She made sure we knew how limited our info is.
She wants us on the back foot.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The Grand Duchess's office is right ahead.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: From the intelligence we gathered beforehand, her name is Elisaveta Konstantinovna Lacitsara.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: She's not the typical Ursine noble. Her policies are known for being kind, to Infected and non-Infected alike.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Every channel of information we've checked describes her as a good person.

options: A woman like that deserves more than just 'kindness'.
The Grand Duchess must also be a bright woman.
Her office is rather humble-looking.
Almost looks like a regular home.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The buildings in Bresk are relatively short and regular. It must be the style here in the Far North.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But looking at the map, all the surrounding buildings seem to almost envelop it. A rather unique location, in terms of urban planning.

options: So, here we are again.
They're not even letting us wait inside this time.
A no-nonsense young lady.
A local leader with quite the reputation.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Are you worried, Doctor?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Honestly speaking, so am I. Even if Eloysius has made her thoughts on the matter clear, we still do not know her true goal—

options: (Shakes head)
Doesn't this all feel rather familiar?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Oh... You mean like in Lungmen?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Ch'en really is no-nonsense, isn't she?

options: Don't you mean 'hard to work with'?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Let's go with 'strict'.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Ch'en treats others the same way she treats herself. That's how it was back then, that's how it is now.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Oh, right! We got news from her before we left home. While she didn't go into detail on her movements, she sounded well.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: When she heard about what happened, she promised that if Rhodes Island needed her, she would return.

options: We've made a lot of friends.
But a lot have left us too.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I still remember when we were working with Ch'en, the one who actually represented Rhodes Island and negotiated with Chief Wei was Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, I'm worried that I won't be able to solve problems or get people to work with us like she did.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Also, we know practically nothing about Ursus's current circumstances, or the Grand Duchess.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, I...

options: We don't need to do what only Kal'tsit could do.
Be yourself, Amiya.
We'll find a way.

steps.name: Far North Soldier
steps.text: May I ask which of you is Dr. {@nickname} of Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Far North Soldier
steps.text: Her Imperial Highness the Grand Duchess invites you to meet with her.
